newsitem.title: BELARUS: Minsk to Moscow - don't overreact to TV crew arrest.
newsitem.headline: Minsk to Moscow - don't overreact to TV crew arrest.

text.p: Belarus Foreign Minister Ivan Antonovich, snubbing a protest by President Boris Yeltsin, told Moscow on Wednesday not to make a political issue out of the detention by Belarus authorities of a Russian television crew.

"Yes, Belarus hears what Russia is saying. But this incident cannot influence important joint policy. The two states have many common problems and Russia has many problems in which it needs Belarussian support," Antonovich told Reuters.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin said earlier on Wednesday the Kremlin might revise a union charter and other accords on closer integration with Belarus if the row was not settled.

Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as asking reporters at the Volzhsky Utyos holiday residence in central Russia to convey his words to Belarus hardline President Alexander Lukashenko: "I am indignant over your actions. I want you to explain what is happening."
Yeltsin said he hoped the incident could be settled, but if it was not, then: "Let us reconsider the charter and the agreements which we have signed". He added: "We do not touch Belarus journalists."
Antonovich responded: "Their president can say harsh words, but that's it. Relations between our countries should not change just because a former ORT correspondent was detained."
